title: Joining Curtis Mosely's band in the Harlem Scandals revue
summary: After the Walkathons he joined Mosely's 13-piece band in a road show with chorus girls and acts, his introduction to show work, playing Chicago theatres and the Midwest.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, in the Walkathon, was that sort of like your first show experience?
That was -- well, to a certain extent.
Because it was pretty low level.

It was low level, but right after I left the Walkathons, and this was about 1933 I left the Walkathons, pardon me, then I joined a big show, a big revue, called the Harlem Scandals. And there was a road show, and we travelled. We travelled all over.
How did you get that gig?
I had just come back to Chicago, and they needed a drummer. This was Curtis Mosely's band, and
Curtis Mosely had had a hell of a band at one time out of Los Angeles. And so they needed a drummer. Because he played drums himself, but he was pretty much over the hill at that particular time.

So they needed a drummer, so I joined them. And chorus girls, 20, 15 chorus girls, and all this type of a thing, and all the different dance teams and acts, big time acts, acts that had played the RKO vaudeville circuit and all of that, Norman Thomas' Quintet, and they had very good acts. And then the show things, and so this was really my introduction to shows, see, then with the big show, we played the Strand and Lake Theatre here in Chicago. We played the Old Stratford Theatre, I don't know whether you remember that, on 63rd Street. And it was a vaudeville house, then. And we played quite a few theatres here in Chicago.
But where -- you say you went on the road with it.

Well, we played everywhere. We played -- well, we played Indianapolis, and then through the state, and then we played the Butterfield Time, that was through the state of Michigan. And then we went West and -- we played practically -- mostly -- most of it was done in the Middle West.
But I was with them about a year, a year and a half.
Was that a big band, or --
Yeah, yeah, he had a big band. It was about 13 pieces. That was big at that particular time.
Did the band have a spot in the show?

Yeah, we did everything, the band did a spot. And then, they had big production numbers. They had a number in there, and it rained on the stage. They had -- they put the tarpaulin in there and then they had a line that they run over the top, then they spotlighted it, and this guy would be singing, 'oh, Lord, please take away the darkness,' and all of that, 'oh, please, take away the rain.' And then it would be raining. It was real first class.
Real big production things. And that was my first introduction. And, young -- you have no fears, you don't know whether you can do anything or not, but you say you can. So I --
Yeah, right, right. Well, you have to -- I had to learn to read, right, right, right. So -- and the band was -- practically the whole band was out of California.
